The '''Chern Institute of Mathematics''' ([[Simplified Chinese characters|Chinese]]: 南开大学陈省身数学研究所; [[pinyin]]: Nánkāi Dàxué Chén Xǐngshēn Shùxué Yánjiūsuǒ) is a research institute at [[Nankai University]] in [[Tianjin]], China. The Institute pursues both pure and applied mathematical research and aims to promote mathematics in China.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Introduction-CIM |url=http://en.cim.nankai.edu.cn/About_CIM/Introduction.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219222902/http://en.cim.nankai.edu.cn/About_CIM/Introduction.htm |archive-date=2025-02-19 |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=en.cim.nankai.edu.cn}}</ref>

== History ==
[[Shiing-Shen Chern]] was invited by China's [[Ministry of Education (China)|Ministry of Education]] to establish a new mathematics research institute at [[Nankai University]] in 1984, two years after Chern had co-founded the Mathematical Sciences Research Institute (now the [[Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute]]) in California.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Hitchin |first=Nigel |author-link=Nigel Hitchin |date=2014 |title=SHIING-SHEN CHERN 26 October 1911 — 3 December 2004 |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/pdf/10.1098/rsbm.2014.0018 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=60 |pages=75-85 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219220401/https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/pdf/10.1098/rsbm.2014.0018 |archive-date=2025-02-19}}</ref>

The Institute was originally named the Nankai Research Institute of Mathematics and was formally opened on 17 October 1985.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Monument of Shiing-Shen Chern and His Wife |url=https://en.nankai.edu.cn/2020/1229/c23107a331556/page.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219220343/https://en.nankai.edu.cn/2020/1229/c23107a331556/page.htm |archive-date=2025-02-19 |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=en.nankai.edu.cn}}</ref> Chern's guiding principle for the Institute was, "based at Nankai, serving the country, and embracing the world."<ref name=":0" />

Chern served as the inaugural director of the Institute until 1992.<ref name=":0" /> Mathematician Guoding Hu served initially as the vice director before taking over from Chern and serving as the director from April 1992 to March 1996.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Guoding Hu -CIM |url=http://en.cim.nankai.edu.cn/info/1034/1149.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219223851/http://en.cim.nankai.edu.cn/info/1034/1149.htm |archive-date=2025-02-19 |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=en.cim.nankai.edu.cn}}</ref>

During his time as director, Chern donated over 10,000 books to the Institute and also prize money of $50,000 from having been awarded the [[Wolf Prize in Mathematics]] in 1984.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

Chern died on 3 December 2004 and the Institute was subsequently renamed in his honour as the Chern Institute of Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web |title="Professor Shiing-Shen Chern's Academic Achievements" — A Special Lecture given by Professor Weiping Zhang-CIM |url=http://en.cim.nankai.edu.cn/info/1141/2203.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219224703/http://en.cim.nankai.edu.cn/info/1141/2203.htm |archive-date=2025-02-19 |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=en.cim.nankai.edu.cn}}</ref>

== Theoretical Physics Division ==
At Chern's request, [[Yang Chen-Ning]] established a Theoretical Physics Division at the Institute in 1986.<ref name=":0" /> The initial major research direction within the Division was [[Yang–Mills theory]] and the [[Yang–Baxter equation]]. Many physicists and mathematicians from around the world have visited and given lectures at the Division, including [[Michael Atiyah]] and [[Freeman Dyson]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Theoretical Physics Division-CIM |url=http://en.cim.nankai.edu.cn/Affiliations/Theoretical_Physics_Division.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219231743/http://en.cim.nankai.edu.cn/Affiliations/Theoretical_Physics_Division.htm |archive-date=2025-02-19 |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=en.cim.nankai.edu.cn}}</ref>

== Visiting Scholars Program ==
In May 2005, the Institute established the Visiting Scholars Program to promote communication and cooperation in mathematical research. Mathematicians from China and the rest of the world can apply to the Institute to conduct research there for a maximum of three months. More than 100 international and domestic scholars conduct research under the program each year.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Visiting Scholars Program-CIM |url=http://en.cim.nankai.edu.cn/Visitors/Visiting_Scholars_Program.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219231058/http://en.cim.nankai.edu.cn/Visitors/Visiting_Scholars_Program.htm |archive-date=2025-02-19 |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=en.cim.nankai.edu.cn}}</ref>
